findings: The May 10 and November 7, 2026 captures are dated versions of the complete five-category Radar rule-attribute reference. Merchants configure rules and Stripe evaluates available inputs. Card issuer checks are post-authorization. The reference distinguishes card charges from supported transaction outcomes and distinguishes Connect transaction actions from action on the connected account itself.

November introduces three recommended scores and retains classic rule predicates. Fraudulent dispute covers cards, ACH Direct Debit and SEPA Direct Debit. Fraudulent payment and early fraud warning scores cover cards only. Each new score is 0–99. The listed classic rule attribute remains 0–100 in both captures, with adjustable default thresholds of 65 for elevated and 75 for highest.

November separates Radar Pro attributes and Treasury rules from the other attribute families. Treasury private preview is limited to certain Radar plans and describes review or block on connected-account Treasury transactions, with inbound transfers, received credits, and inbound/return aggregates.

The source summary covers the core categorization, classic score values, fingerprint, and early-access crypto. Its 32-currency claim undercounts the 34 enumerated currencies in both captures. Its cross-method row should describe shared applicability that can vary by attribute. Keep cards, ACH and SEPA on the specific fingerprint route.
substantive_changes: November adds the three recommended scores and their payment method scopes, expands customer guidance with a Dashboard enrollment route for eligible Accounts v2 preview users while keeping a preview version requirement, and documents the shared iCloud Private Relay IP counter caveat with optional rule exclusion.

New rows identify Stripe-detected free-trial transactions primarily from Checkout or Billing and Stripe-identified AI-agent-initiated card payments. Radar Pro adds card bot, free-trial abuse and refund abuse scores or levels, plus comparison of supplied cardholder name to Stripe-inferred names with explicit match/unavailable/not-provided outcomes.

Liability shift remains approximate. May frames preauthorization true for non-wallet card payments and possible false for certain digital wallets. November describes a card payment with preauthorization liability shift, later network downgrade, and possible false for some Google Pay payments.

November lists platform transaction rules for destination, direct and separate charges/transfers, with the overarching charge type and Radar tier condition. Account rules depend on tier. It adds the Treasury private preview branch, and its account rules show account_fraud_risk_level and account_fraud_risk_score, with account_risk_level appearing separately under Treasury rules. No runtime rename or universal direct-charge access was demonstrated.
Table alignment, inline markup, explicit Description headers, headings with whitespace and a change to the ISP row example are presentation. Rules and Rules Reference remain navigation.

The November digital_wallet predicate lists network_token, absent from the May row. Both rows require a registered-device cryptogram for the listed values and expressly exempt android_pay, which is valid with or without it.
historical_claims_to_preserve: May's direct-charge Radar for Platforms condition and account-rule Radar for Platforms restriction are dated documentary evidence. Preserve the two captures' wording and route to risk settings for platform controls.

May documented account_risk_level in account rules. May also listed twelve yearly transaction counters covering customers, distinct emails, cards and names. November omits those yearly rows but retains related shorter windows and several charges-only or differently scoped yearly counters.

Both retain early access for email commonality and the three crypto fields, public preview for the card description, issuer and 3DS-result fields, missing non-Boolean predicates outside the relevant payment method, and the deprecated payment transaction_type exception for Request Credentials. Keep the latter distinct from Treasury transaction_type.
conflicts: The current summary's 32 currencies conflicts with the 34 currencies actually enumerated at May line 60 and November line 66. Preserve the base-unit rule for decimal currencies.

The Radar concept's Risk Settings and Controls and Risk Levels and Scoring use 0–99, and its score table labels risk_score deprecated. The supported-attributes reference gives 0–100 in both captures and November says classic predicates remain supported. Separate the 0–99 Risk Settings model presentation and the default high-risk block-rule deprecation from classic rule-attribute support. The related November Risk Settings raw lines 141–156 explicitly permit continued custom rules on risk_score.

The Radar concept's built-in rule text uses account_risk_level, a May account-rule name. November's account-rules rows use account_fraud_risk_level and account_fraud_risk_score, while its Treasury rules document account_risk_level. Date and scope each name rather than collapsing them.

Within both captures, refund_count_on_card_all_time describes a billing address while companion windows refer to a card. Both copies also describe usd_amount_disputed_for_account_daily as past week and the monthly/weekly usd_amount_refunded_for_account rows as past day, in each of the two platform rule sections. Preserve these as documentation ambiguities.

The Radar concept describes bot_score as Checkout-only at lines 159 and 204. November Supported Attributes lines 207–213 state Radar Pro and cards only. The separate November Bot Abuse raw lines 11–17 name Stripe Checkout, Custom Checkout, Radar Sessions and Web Elements, with Radar Pro including the score. Keep both the method and integration scopes, without extrapolating to other card integrations.
unresolved_questions: The two dated captures do not settle whether omitted yearly counters still evaluate, whether old and new account-risk names can coexist or migrate automatically, or which account-level entitlements changed. The related November Risk Settings raw lines 158–183 document that platform direct-charge rules depend on merchant-of-record and platform controls.

The published raw descriptions leave the counting entity of refund_count_on_card_all_time and the actual windows of the inconsistent platform amount rows unresolved. No runtime behavior is established from those contradictions.

The Supported Attributes and Risk Settings pages describe different range endings for classic risk. Preserve each source's context and avoid treating the documented 0–100 rule-attribute range as proof that the model emits 100.

findings: Add a dated November evidence route and concise discoverability for recommended scores, Accounts v2 and relay caveats, Radar Pro and Connect/Treasury rule scopes. Keep the May reference accessible for historical names and yearly counters.
Record the November addition of network_token to the digital_wallet values, with the cryptogram condition and android_pay exception intact.
conflicts: Correct the currency count or route readers to the explicit list. Preserve score-range and default-rule deprecation distinctions, dated platform eligibility and account-attribute namespace, and the inconsistent refund entity and period descriptions.

Separate classic rule-attribute range from Risk Settings model range and default-rule retirement. Replace the Radar concept's stale Checkout-only bot-score wording with dated method, tier and integration scopes.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/radar/rules/supported-attributes, source-stripe-radar-rules-supported-attributes should describe the November 7, 2026 capture as a five-category attribute catalog for merchants writing Radar rules. Stripe supplies the payment and account signals, and method-specific non-Boolean inputs are missing for other methods. Card issuers supply the post-authorization address and CVC checks. The outcome counters distinguish card charge data from supported transaction outcomes, including authorization, block, decline and total with row-specific setup scope. The fingerprint family applies to cards, ACH and SEPA. See new raw lines 17-29, new raw lines 218-254, new raw lines 375-381, new raw lines 450-455, new raw lines 488-509 and new raw lines 596-617. May documents the same basic scope and timing in old raw lines 16-28, old raw lines 202-238, old raw lines 366-372 and old raw lines 441-446. November recommends 0–99 fraudulent dispute scores for cards/ACH Direct Debit/SEPA Direct Debit and 0–99 early fraud warning and fraudulent payment scores for cards, while retaining classic risk rules and their adjustable 65/75 defaults. May and the existing summary list the classic score only. See old raw lines 30-35 and new raw lines 31-41. For Connect, platform transaction rules support review, block or allow on connected-account transactions, and account rules can submit the connected account itself for review. The separate Treasury branch supports review or block of Treasury transactions for connected accounts in private preview on certain plans. The November capture also documents the Accounts v2 preview version and Dashboard enrollment condition, Radar Pro attributes, Stripe-detected free-trial transactions primarily from Checkout/Billing, and Stripe-identified AI-agent-initiated payments under Cards. See old raw lines 8-14, old raw lines 664-677, old raw lines 748-756, new raw lines 9-15, new raw line 178, new raw lines 207-216, new raw line 402, new raw lines 673-687, new raw lines 758-767 and new raw lines 835-881. The summary's five-category and fingerprint map remains useful, its currency count needs correction, and its old-only scope leaves the November additions undiscoverable.
